comparison_podded_vs_conventional.note: Same hull, same added mass, same cross-flow and resistance model; the only difference is the steering/thrust hardware. This is a like-for-like internal comparison, NOT a comparison against SIMMAN (see criteria[criterion_3]).

conventional.note: advance / D_T are geometry indicators measured inside the first half turn and do not require a steady state; the kinematic 2u/r diameter is only a consistency check of the settled turn

podded.note: advance / D_T are geometry indicators measured inside the first half turn and do not require a steady state; the kinematic 2u/r diameter is only a consistency check of the settled turn

limitations: Hull forces are a DECLARED SNAME-prime derivative set (linear + quadratic), not a transcribed PMM table: no digit-exact KVLCC2 derivative set exists offline (see the anchor blocked block). Absolute accuracy is WITHHELD.

Constant-azimuth pod model: the thrust-vector yaw moment does not decay with drift the way a rudder's does (the rudder's effective incidence falls as the drift builds). Consequently the podded 35 deg circle settles into a tight spiral (u -> 0.11 u0, kinematic 2u/r diameter 0.24 L) instead of a wide steady circle. The IMO indicators are measured inside the first half turn (advance at 90 deg, tactical diameter at 180 deg) and are therefore still defined, but the podded steady speed/drift must not be read as a podded-tanker speed loss.
No drift-induced longitudinal resistance (X_vv = X_vr = 0), no heel/roll coupling, no free surface, no shaft-power limit (the propeller speed is held at its self-propulsion value).
Ice is a declared scenario parameter (an extra steady resistance as a fraction of R(U0)); no ice-hull or ice-pod contact physics, no added mass from ice, no channel/broken-channel asymmetry.

IMO overshoot limits are a grade-B transcription (in-ecosystem transcription of Res. MSC.137(76) annex 2.3); one label conflict between two in-ecosystem sources is recorded and left unresolved (anchor conflicts block).
